details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:679 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The guard is gated by `[ "${HEAL_ROUTE:-false}" != true ]`, so it is skipped on the heal route, where auto-heal remediation runs go.
  WHY: Auto-heal remediation issues are routed with HEAL_ROUTE=true, so the guard never blocks the no-code PRs it was written to stop. Severity disagreement: minimax says BLOCKER; gemini says MAJOR (confidence 2) and is unsure whether the bypass is intended; sonnet and glm judged it intended.
- scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:680-681 | severity=major | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The staged-path list uses `--diff-filter=ACMRD`, which omits type-changed (`T`) paths.
  WHY: If type-changed paths are the whole staged set, the guard is skipped; in a mixed set they are not counted. Severity disagreement: sonnet and glm say NIT; gemini and luna say MAJOR.
- scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:680 | severity=nit | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Non-ASCII staged paths are C-quoted under the default core.quotePath and are classified as code.
  WHY: A remediation that changes only non-ASCII-named doc or test files is treated as a code change, so the guard fails open and the no-code PR is opened.
- scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:603-641 | severity=major | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `db/contracts/` is treated as non-code, although `is_auto_heal_companion_path` allows it as a companion path.
  WHY: A legitimate DB-contract-only fix is parked as no-code and the alert stays open. Sonnet and glm judged this intended per the PR description.
- scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:677-678 | severity=major | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The guard is skipped whenever `PRIOR_PR_BASELINE_BRANCH` is non-empty, with no check that the baseline branch holds a code change.
  WHY: A reissue that stages only docs or tests on a no-code baseline still opens a no-code PR. Severity disagreement: minimax says MAJOR; glm says NIT (confidence 2). Gemini raised this as a task gap.
- scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:678 | severity=major | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: If printf fails (rc 126), the case statement's default branch logs a warning and lets the commit proceed.
  WHY: The guard is bypassed when the path list cannot be determined. Sonnet and glm treat this as the intended documented fail-open.
- scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:689-721 | severity=nit | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The helper's stderr is redirected to /dev/null, so fail-open paths and Python tracebacks are not diagnosable from the log.
  WHY: A helper regression yields only a generic warning with the exit code.
- scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:644-661 | severity=nit | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The shell's `^[a-z_]+$` sanitisation rewrites a helper reason containing a hyphen to `unknown`.
  WHY: This hides a helper regression behind the same log value as a crash.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_report.sh:185-196 | severity=nit | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The jq filter assumes comments arrive in chronological order.
  WHY: If the API reorders comments, the wrong rejection marker could be picked and a heal dispatch not skipped.
- agents.d/audit-2026-11-remediation-no-code-guard.md:file name | severity=nit | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The fragment slug has a date prefix and no issue or PR number, contrary to §25. Minimax also flags the matching changelog.d fragment.
  WHY: This departs from the `<issue-or-pr>-<slug>.md` naming convention. Sonnet found existing fragments with the same shape.
- scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:660-729 | severity=nit | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The guard returns early unless REMEDIATION_NO_CODE_GUARD_ENABLED equals "true", so its own default is off.
  WHY: §8 requires the default to live in the helper. Sonnet and glm checked and found the default is `true`.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: An implement run for an auto-heal remediation issue now stops before the commit when every staged path is a doc, test, fragment or DB contract path; the motivating PRs 5343/5345/5346/5347 changed only README and tests.
  expected_change_site: scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:679 (HEAL_ROUTE gating of the guard)
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The guard has `HEAL_ROUTE != true` as its first condition, auto-heal remediation issues run with HEAL_ROUTE=true (scripts/implement_heal_preflight.sh:314), and the unit test asserts allow on the heal route.
- requirement: The fail-open catalogue lists missing issue body, empty staged set and prior-PR branch runs, and the marker line is the only trigger.
  expected_change_site: scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:675-679
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The PR description's fail-open catalogue omits the heal-route skip, which only the agents.d fragment lists. The heal-route skip and the marker check cannot coexist, so the guard is effectively dead code.
- requirement: Auto-heal remediation runs that change no code must be stopped before a PR is opened, with no skip that lets a no-code run open a PR.
  expected_change_site: scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh commit-path guard, and the baseline env wiring at implement.yml:5534
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  EVIDENCE: The skip on a non-empty PRIOR_PR_BASELINE_BRANCH has no code-content test, and no other no-code check exists on the baseline path.
- requirement: "When every staged path is a doc, test, fragment or DB contract path... nothing is committed, no PR is opened and no review runs."
  expected_change_site: scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh and implement_handle_guard_block.sh
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  EVIDENCE: Nothing verifies that the whole workflow handles the abort without triggering Review & Autofix or other downstream artefacts; only the commit and push are blocked.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:680 | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The staged-path list drops type-changed (`T`) paths and uses the default core.quotePath, unlike the guard at line 524. Non-ASCII names are C-quoted and classified as code, and type changes are not listed.
  WHY: The first case fails open and the second fails closed, so a no-code remediation can still be allowed. Both are rare. The fix is `git -c core.quotePath=false diff --cached --name-only --no-renames --diff-filter=ACMRDT`.
- scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:689-720 | severity=nit | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Any helper exit other than 0 or 40 logs a warning with `reason=helper_error` and the commit proceeds, and the helper's stderr is discarded.
  WHY: This is a diagnosability nit, not a defect. The reviewer did not confirm that rc=126 is a bypass; it is the documented fail-open.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:680 | severity=major | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The staged-path list is built with `--diff-filter=ACMRD`, which omits type-change (T) paths.
  WHY: A remediation whose staged set holds only type-changed non-code files bypasses the guard and opens a PR.
- scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:is_remediation_non_code_path | severity=major | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: db/contracts/ is treated as a non-code path.
  WHY: A necessary DB contract fix is parked as no-code, and the pipeline stops without applying it.
- scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:678 | severity=major | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Failure handling for printf failure is insufficient.
  WHY: A printf failure gives rc 126, which hits the default case, logs a warning and lets the commit proceed, bypassing the guard.
- scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:660-729 | severity=major | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The guard returns early when HEAL_ROUTE is set.
  WHY: It is unclear whether heal-route remediation runs should be guarded; if they should, the guard never fires and the no-code PR is opened.
- scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:is_remediation_non_code_path | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Non-ASCII staged paths come out C-quoted under the default core.quotePath.
  WHY: The guard classifies any quoted string as code, so a non-ASCII doc or test-only remediation is misclassified.
- scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:689-693 | severity=nit | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Fail-open paths are invisible in the logs.
  WHY: Stderr goes to /dev/null and helper exits other than 0 or 40 proceed silently.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_report.sh:185-196 | severity=nit | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The jq filter assumes comments are returned in chronological order.
  WHY: If the API reorders comments, the wrong rejection marker could be picked and a heal dispatch not skipped.
- agents.d/audit-2026-11-remediation-no-code-guard.md:file name | severity=nit | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The fragment slug is date-prefixed with no issue or PR number.
  WHY: This departs from the §25 naming convention.
- scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:660-729 | severity=nit | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The helper returns early unless REMEDIATION_NO_CODE_GUARD_ENABLED equals "true", so its own default is off.
  WHY: §8 requires the helper to carry its own default.
- TASK_GAP: requirement: auto-heal remediation runs that change no code must be stopped before a PR is opened, with no skip that lets a no-code run open a PR.
  expected_change_site: scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh commit-path guard, and the baseline env wiring at implement.yml:5534
  EVIDENCE: The skip on a non-empty PRIOR_PR_BASELINE_BRANCH has no code-content test. No other no-code check was found on the baseline path.
  severity=major | confidence=3
- TASK_GAP: requirement: "When every staged path is a doc, test, fragment or DB contract path... nothing is committed, no PR is opened and no review runs."
  expected_change_site: scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh and the associated handler
  EVIDENCE: Nothing verifies that the workflow handles the abort without triggering Review & Autofix or other secondary artefacts; only the commit and push are blocked.
  severity=major | confidence=3
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:679 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The guard is gated by `HEAL_ROUTE != true`, but auto-heal remediation issues always run with HEAL_ROUTE=true (scripts/implement_heal_preflight.sh:314), so the guard never runs on the path it was designed to catch.
  WHY: The helper would return `block`, but the shell never reaches it, so the pre-push gate pushes the no-code PR and defeats the PR's purpose.
- scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:603,641 | severity=major | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: All of `db/contracts/` is treated as non-code, contradicting `_AUTO_HEAL_CONTRACT_RE` and `is_auto_heal_companion_path` (lines 562-570), which allow those paths as code.
  WHY: A remediation that only updates a DB contract is parked with `ai:scope-blocked`, the alert stays open, and a human must redispatch.
- scripts/implement_commit_chan
